trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Rome
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: No morning activities — flight arrives at 13:00. Use the time on board to rest.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Rome Fiumicino Airport at 13:00. Take the Leonardo Express train to Roma Termini (€14, ~32 min), then connect via metro/bus to Vatican City/Borgo district. Check in to your boutique stay, freshen up, and take a relaxed stroll along Via della Conciliazione toward St. Peter's Square — admire the stunning colonnade and the exterior of St. Peter's Basilica for free. Explore the charming Borgo Pio pedestrian street nearby.
day_by_day.evening: Wander through the Castel Sant'Angelo area at dusk for beautiful free views of the Tiber River and the illuminated fortress. Enjoy the golden-hour atmosphere along the riverbanks.

meals.breakfast: Eat on the plane or grab a quick espresso and cornetto (€2–3) at a bar near the airport or Termini station upon arrival.
meals.lunch: Grab a quick and affordable slice of pizza al taglio near Termini or in the Borgo area (€3–5) after checking in.
meals.dinner: Trattoria da Lucia del Borgo on Borgo Pio — a neighborhood gem with hearty Roman pasta dishes like cacio e pepe or amatriciana for €8–12. Alternatively, try a local pizzeria on Borgo Pio for a sit-down pizza under €10.

day_by_day.notes: Day 1 is intentionally light given the afternoon arrival. Focus on settling in and getting oriented. Purchase a 48-hour or 72-hour Roma Pass if you plan to use public transport heavily (€28–38). Validate all metro/bus tickets before boarding.

day_by_day.morning: Early visit to St. Peter's Basilica (free entry, opens 7:00 AM) — arrive before 9:00 AM to beat the crowds. Climb to the top of the dome for panoramic views of Rome (€8 on foot, €10 by elevator). Spend time admiring Michelangelo's Pietà and the breathtaking interior.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Vatican Museums and Sistine Chapel (book tickets online in advance to avoid queues, ~€20 for standard entry). Marvel at the Gallery of Maps, Raphael Rooms, and the awe-inspiring Sistine Chapel ceiling. Afterward, walk along the ancient Aurelian Walls nearby.
day_by_day.evening: Cross the Tiber via Ponte Sant'Angelo and explore the lively Campo de' Fiori square. Browse the evening atmosphere, street musicians, and watch locals gather.

meals.breakfast: Bar/café near the hotel — espresso + cornetto (€2–3). Try Caffè San Pietro on Via della Conciliazione for an authentic Roman breakfast.
meals.lunch: Picnic-style lunch from a local alimentari (deli) near the Vatican — grab fresh bread, local cheese, cured meats, and fruit for €6–8 total. Eat in the nearby Piazza del Risorgimento.
meals.dinner: Osteria dell'Angelo near Prati district — famous for traditional Roman Thursday-style cuisine (note: check weekly specials). Budget €12–15 for a full meal with house wine. Alternatively, try any trattoria in the Prati neighborhood for pasta and a carafe of house wine under €15.

day_by_day.notes: Book Vatican Museums tickets online at least 2–3 days in advance to save time and sometimes money on skip-the-line fees. Dress code applies for St. Peter's Basilica — covered shoulders and knees required. Bring a scarf or light layer.

day_by_day.morning: Take the metro (Line A) or bus to the Spanish Steps (Trinità dei Monti) — free to visit and stunning in the morning light. Walk down to the Trevi Fountain (10-minute walk) and toss a coin for good luck. Explore the elegant Baroque fountain and the surrounding streets.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk to the Pantheon (€5 entry, one of the world's best-preserved ancient buildings) — budget 45–60 minutes inside. Afterward, explore the charming Piazza Navona (free), admiring Bernini's Fountain of the Four Rivers and street artists. Browse the surrounding medieval alleyways.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Trastevere neighborhood via bus (15–20 min from city center) for a vibrant, bohemian evening atmosphere. Explore the cobblestone streets, visit the beautiful Santa Maria in Trastevere basilica (free, open evenings), and enjoy the lively piazza.

meals.breakfast: Local bar near the hotel — cappuccino + pastry (€2.50–3.50).
meals.lunch: Lunch near the Pantheon area — try Pizzarium-style pizza al taglio or a falafel wrap from a street vendor for €4–6. Avoid sit-down restaurants directly on Piazza della Rotonda (tourist markup).
meals.dinner: Trastevere is perfect for budget dining — try Da Enzo al 29 or Tonnarello for classic Roman dishes (cacio e pepe, carbonara, supplì). Budget €12–16 for a full dinner with local wine.

day_by_day.notes: The Trevi Fountain is best visited early morning or late evening to avoid peak crowds. Trastevere gets busy on weekday evenings — arrive by 7:00 PM to get a table without a long wait at popular spots. Bus routes 23 or 280 connect Trastevere to the Vatican area easily.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Colosseum, Roman Forum, and Palatine Hill (combined ticket ~€16, book online in advance). Arrive at opening time (9:00 AM) to beat the heat and crowds. Spend 2–3 hours exploring ancient Rome's most iconic landmark and the sprawling Forum ruins.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk up Capitoline Hill (Campidoglio) for a free panoramic view over the Roman Forum. Visit the Capitoline Museums (€15 — Rome's oldest public museums, home to the original Marcus Aurelius statue and Caravaggio works). Alternatively, save the museums for another day and explore the Circus Maximus and Aventine Hill (free) — see the famous Knights of Malta keyhole view of St. Peter's dome.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the Prati district (near your hotel) for a relaxed evening. Walk along the Tiber embankment at sunset and enjoy gelato from a local gelateria.

meals.breakfast: Café near the hotel — standard Roman breakfast (€2.50–3).
meals.lunch: Pack a picnic or grab street food near the Colosseum — avoid tourist traps directly outside. Walk 5 minutes to find a local bar or alimentari for a panino and water (€4–6).
meals.dinner: Prati neighborhood near your hotel — try Il Sorpasso or any neighborhood trattoria for Roman classics. Budget €10–14 for pasta, a glass of wine, and bread.

day_by_day.notes: The Colosseum combined ticket includes the Roman Forum and Palatine Hill — great value. Wear comfortable walking shoes as the terrain is uneven. Bring water and sunscreen, especially in June when temperatures can exceed 30°C (86°F). Book Colosseum tickets online to avoid 1–2 hour queues.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the Borghese Gallery (€15, reservations MANDATORY — book weeks in advance as slots are limited). One of Rome's finest art museums, housing Bernini sculptures and Caravaggio masterpieces in a gorgeous villa. Entry is timed at 2-hour intervals. Afterward, stroll through the beautiful Villa Borghese gardens (free) — Rome's version of Central Park.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk or take the bus to the Piazza del Popolo (free) — admire the twin baroque churches and the Egyptian obelisk. Climb the Pincian Hill terrace (free) for one of the best panoramic views of Rome. Explore the nearby Flaminio district and the MAXXI contemporary art museum exterior (or enter for ~€12 if budget allows).
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a Friday evening passeggiata (evening stroll) along Via del Corso and the surrounding streets. Window shop, people-watch, and soak up the Roman evening energy.

meals.breakfast: Try a different local café today — espresso standing at the bar is always cheapest (€1–1.50). Grab a maritozzo (Roman cream bun) for a local treat (€2–3).
meals.lunch: Picnic in Villa Borghese gardens — buy supplies from a nearby alimentari or market: fruit, cheese, bread, and a small bottle of water for €6–8.
meals.dinner: Head back toward the Prati or Borgo area — try Pizzarium by Gabriele Bonci on Via della Meloria (a short walk from the Vatican area), widely regarded as Rome's best pizza al taglio. A generous portion costs €5–8. Perfect budget Friday dinner.

day_by_day.notes: Borghese Gallery reservations are essential — book as early as possible online at galleriaborghese.it. The gallery limits visitors to 360 per session. Villa Borghese is a wonderful free escape from the city heat — bring a blanket for the gardens.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Testaccio neighborhood — Rome's authentic working-class food district. Explore the Testaccio Market (Mercato di Testaccio, open until 2:00 PM, free to enter) for fresh produce, local cheeses, cured meats, street food, and Roman specialties like supplì and porchetta sandwiches. A paradise for food lovers on a budget.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk to the non-Catholic Cemetery (Cimitero Acattolico, €3 suggested donation) where Keats and Shelley are buried — a surprisingly beautiful and peaceful spot. Nearby, see the Pyramid of Cestius (exterior, free) — a genuine ancient Egyptian-style pyramid in Rome. Explore the Ostiense district street art scene (free).
day_by_day.evening: Return to Trastevere or explore the Gianicolo Hill (Janiculum) at sunset — the best free panoramic viewpoint in Rome, with a stunning 180-degree view of the entire city. The cannon fires here daily at noon (worth catching if nearby).

meals.breakfast: Eat at the Testaccio Market — grab a fresh cornetto or a Roman street food breakfast for €2–4.
meals.lunch: Lunch at the Testaccio Market stalls — try a supplì (fried rice ball, €2), a porchetta sandwich (€4), and fresh seasonal fruit. Total budget: €6–9 for a fantastic local food experience.
meals.dinner: Trattoria in Testaccio — try Flavio al Velavevodetto or Da Remo (famous for thin-crust Roman pizza). Budget €10–15 for a full meal. Saturday evenings are lively — book ahead or arrive early.

day_by_day.notes: Testaccio Market is a highlight for food lovers — bring cash as many stalls don't accept cards. Saturday is a great day to experience authentic Roman neighborhood life away from tourist crowds. The Gianicolo viewpoint is accessible by bus 115 from Trastevere.

day_by_day.morning: Sunday morning in Rome is magical — visit the Porta Portese flea market in Trastevere (open Sunday 6:00 AM – 2:00 PM, free entry), one of Europe's largest and most famous flea markets. Browse vintage clothing, antiques, books, and Roman curiosities. Great for affordable souvenirs.
day_by_day.afternoon: Last afternoon in Rome — revisit any favorite spots or explore the Jewish Ghetto (free to walk, fascinating history) and the nearby Teatro di Marcello (exterior, free — often called Rome's 'other Colosseum'). Stop by the Largo di Torre Argentina (free outdoor ruins where Julius Caesar was assassinated). End with a final gelato from a quality gelateria (avoid places with piled-high fluorescent gelato — look for metal lids covering the gelato, a sign of quality).
day_by_day.evening: Final dinner in Rome — treat yourself slightly with a sit-down meal at a neighborhood trattoria near your hotel in Borgo or Prati. Pack bags for departure and do a final stroll along the Tiber by Castel Sant'Angelo under the evening lights.

meals.breakfast: Last Roman café breakfast — espresso and cornetto (€2.50–3). Savor the ritual of standing at the bar like a local.
meals.lunch: Light lunch near the Jewish Ghetto — try the famous Roman-Jewish fried artichokes (carciofi alla giudia, €6–8) at a local trattoria, or grab street food near Campo de' Fiori.
meals.dinner: Splurge slightly on your final night — budget €15–20 for a full Roman meal with antipasto, pasta, and house wine at a well-rated Prati trattoria. Try Il Sorpasso or Osteria dell'Angelo for a memorable farewell dinner.

day_by_day.notes: Porta Portese gets very crowded by 9:00 AM — arrive early for the best finds and cooler temperatures. Keep an eye on your belongings in crowded market areas. For souvenirs, avoid tourist shops near major monuments (overpriced) — the flea market and Testaccio Market offer far better value. Check your flight details for Day 8 departure logistics.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival & Hotel Check-In: Flight lands at 13:00, so morning is in transit. Take the Leonardo Express train from Fiumicino Airport to Roma Termini, then connect via taxi or bus to your boutique hotel in the Borgo district near Vatican City. Check in, freshen up, and get oriented in the neighborhood.
day_by_day.afternoon: Neighborhood Orientation Walk: Stroll through the Borgo Pio pedestrian street, explore the Castel Sant'Angelo exterior and the scenic Ponte Sant'Angelo with its angel sculptures over the Tiber. Get your first iconic Roman views without the pressure of a full tour. Pick up a gelato from a nearby gelateria to beat the June heat.
day_by_day.evening: Trastevere Food & Wine Evening Walk: Join the guided Trastevere Food & Wine Evening Walk — a perfect low-effort, high-reward first evening. Wander cobblestone streets sampling supplì (Roman rice balls), cacio e pepe bites, local wines, and more. A festive, delicious introduction to Roman food culture.

meals.breakfast: On the plane or grab a quick cornetto and cappuccino at the airport or Termini station upon arrival.
meals.lunch: Light lunch near Fiumicino or at a café in the Borgo district after check-in — try a simple panino or pizza al taglio at a local bakery (€8–12).
meals.dinner: Covered by the Trastevere Food & Wine Evening Walk (street food tastings included). Supplement with a glass of local wine at a Trastevere wine bar if still hungry.

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 light — jet lag and travel fatigue are real. The Trastevere walk starts in the early evening (typically 18:00–19:00), giving you time to rest first. Confirm exact meeting point when booking. Wear comfortable walking shoes.

day_by_day.morning: Vatican Museums & Sistine Chapel: Book the first entry slot (8:00 or 9:00) to beat the crowds. Explore the Gallery of Maps, Raphael Rooms, and culminate in Michelangelo's awe-inspiring Sistine Chapel ceiling. Allow 3–4 hours for a thorough but comfortable visit.
day_by_day.afternoon: St. Peter's Basilica & Square: Directly adjacent to the Museums, enter St. Peter's Basilica for free — admire Michelangelo's Pietà, the grand nave, and Bernini's baldachin. Optionally climb the dome for panoramic city views (€8 with elevator). Afterward, relax in St. Peter's Square with a cold drink.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner in the Prati neighborhood: Head to the lively Prati district (a short walk from your hotel) for a sit-down dinner at a traditional Roman trattoria. Enjoy classic dishes like cacio e pepe, carbonara, or artichokes alla romana.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at your boutique hotel or a nearby café — cornetto and cappuccino, the classic Roman start (€3–6).
meals.lunch: Quick lunch inside or just outside the Vatican Museums — try the museum café or grab pizza al taglio from a nearby bakery on Via Cola di Rienzo (€10–15).
meals.dinner: Trattoria in Prati — recommended: Trattoria Il Sorpasso or similar. Expect €25–40 per person with wine.

day_by_day.notes: Pre-book Vatican Museums tickets well in advance — June is peak season and same-day tickets are nearly impossible. A guided tour or skip-the-line ticket is strongly recommended. Dress code enforced: no bare shoulders or knees inside the Basilica.

day_by_day.morning: Borghese Gallery Art Experience: Take a taxi or tram to the Villa Borghese park for your reserved slot at the Borghese Gallery (entry is strictly timed, 9:00 or 11:00 slots). Marvel at Bernini's dynamic sculptures — Apollo and Daphne, The Rape of Proserpina — and Caravaggio's dramatic canvases. Allow 2 hours inside.
day_by_day.afternoon: Villa Borghese Park & Spanish Steps: After the gallery, enjoy a leisurely walk through the beautiful Villa Borghese gardens. Descend to the Spanish Steps (Trinità dei Monti) and explore the upscale Via Condotti area. Window shop or browse the Tridente neighborhood. Visit the Trevi Fountain (a 15-minute walk) and toss your coin.
day_by_day.evening: Cooking Class — Handmade Pasta & Tiramisu: Join the small-group evening cooking class in a historic Roman kitchen. Learn to make fresh pasta from scratch and the perfect tiramisu. A hands-on, social, and delicious way to spend the evening — dinner is the class itself!

meals.breakfast: Café breakfast near the hotel — try Caffè San Pietro or similar Borgo-area café for a proper Roman breakfast (€4–7).
meals.lunch: Picnic-style lunch in Villa Borghese park — pick up fresh bread, cheese, prosciutto, and fruit from a nearby deli or the Mercato Trionfale market (€10–15).
meals.dinner: Included in the Cooking Class — you eat what you make! Paired with Italian wines. (Class fee covers this meal.)

day_by_day.notes: Borghese Gallery requires advance reservations — it sells out weeks ahead in June. Maximum 360 visitors per 2-hour slot. The cooking class typically runs 18:00–21:00; confirm timing when booking. A truly memorable combination of art and food in one day.

day_by_day.morning: Ancient Rome — Colosseum, Roman Forum & Palatine Hill: Take a bus or metro to the Colosseum. Book a skip-the-line combo ticket covering the Colosseum, Roman Forum, and Palatine Hill. Spend the morning walking through 2,000 years of history — the gladiatorial arena, the ancient city center, and the imperial palaces.
day_by_day.afternoon: Capitoline Hill & Capitoline Museums: Walk up to the Capitoline Hill (Campidoglio) designed by Michelangelo. Visit the Capitoline Museums — the world's oldest public museums — housing Marcus Aurelius's equestrian statue, the Capitoline Wolf, and stunning ancient sculptures. Enjoy rooftop views over the Roman Forum.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner in Testaccio neighborhood: Head to Testaccio, Rome's authentic working-class food district, for dinner. Try a classic Roman trattoria serving offal-based dishes (pajata, trippa) or stick to safer classics like amatriciana and abbacchio. Lively, authentic, and affordable.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a nearby bar — fuel up well before a big walking day.
meals.lunch: Street food near the Colosseum or a quick stop at a tavola calda (Roman hot food bar) — suppli, pizza, or a simple pasta (€10–15). Avoid overpriced tourist traps directly beside the Colosseum.
meals.dinner: Testaccio trattoria — try Flavio al Velavevodetto or Da Remo (for pizza). Budget €20–35 per person.

day_by_day.notes: This is the most walking-intensive day — wear very comfortable shoes and bring water. June heat can be intense by midday; the Capitoline Museums offer a cool afternoon refuge. Book Colosseum tickets in advance online.

day_by_day.morning: Testaccio Market & Offal Food Tour: Start early at the Testaccio covered market for the guided food tour. Explore stalls with local vendors, taste Roman street food, learn about offal traditions, cured meats, cheeses, and seasonal produce. An immersive deep-dive into authentic Roman culinary culture.
day_by_day.afternoon: Aventine Hill & Orange Garden: After the food tour, walk up the Aventine Hill to the peaceful Giardino degli Aranci (Orange Garden) with its famous keyhole view of St. Peter's dome perfectly framed through the Knights of Malta garden gate. Visit the ancient Basilica of Santa Sabina. A tranquil, photogenic, and crowd-free afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset Aperitivo & Dinner in Trastevere: Cross the Tiber into Trastevere for a classic Roman aperitivo hour (Campari Spritz or Aperol with nibbles at a piazza bar), followed by dinner at a charming Trastevere restaurant with outdoor seating.

meals.breakfast: Light — the food tour begins with tastings, so skip a heavy breakfast. Just a coffee before heading out.
meals.lunch: Covered by the Testaccio Market Food Tour tastings — you'll be well fed! Optionally grab a light supplemental bite at the market (€5–8 extra).
meals.dinner: Trastevere restaurant — try Da Enzo al 29 or Tonnarello for classic Roman dishes with a lively atmosphere. Budget €25–40 per person with wine.

day_by_day.notes: The Testaccio Market tour typically runs 9:00–12:00. The Aventine keyhole (Piazza dei Cavalieri di Malta) is free and one of Rome's best-kept secrets — arrive before the small queue forms. Trastevere on a Friday evening is lively and festive.

day_by_day.morning: Piazza Navona, Pantheon & Campo de' Fiori: Explore Rome's beautiful baroque heart. Start at Piazza Navona (Bernini's Fountain of the Four Rivers), walk to the magnificent Pantheon (book timed entry, €5), then browse the Campo de' Fiori morning market for flowers, spices, and local produce.
day_by_day.afternoon: Jewish Ghetto & Largo di Torre Argentina: Explore Rome's ancient Jewish Ghetto neighborhood with its history and excellent kosher-influenced Roman cuisine. Visit Largo di Torre Argentina — the ancient temple ruins where Julius Caesar was assassinated (now with a free cat sanctuary). Browse the antique and artisan shops of the area.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell Splurge Dinner near the Pantheon: Treat yourself to a slightly elevated dinner at a well-regarded restaurant in the historic center — enjoy Roman classics elevated with quality ingredients and excellent local wine. A memorable penultimate evening.

meals.breakfast: Saturday morning café ritual — sit down at a Prati café for a leisurely cornetto and cappuccino before heading out (€4–7).
meals.lunch: Lunch in the Jewish Ghetto — try the famous carciofi alla giudia (Jewish-style fried artichokes) and filetti di baccalà at a local trattoria (€15–25 per person).
meals.dinner: Elevated mid-range dinner near Piazza Navona or the Pantheon — try Osteria dell'Ingegno or similar. Budget €35–50 per person with wine.

day_by_day.notes: The Pantheon now requires a timed reservation (€5 entry fee). Saturday mornings at Campo de' Fiori are vibrant but crowded. The Jewish Ghetto area is quieter and more authentic — a wonderful contrast. Book dinner in advance for Saturday evening.

day_by_day.morning: Slow Sunday Morning — Local Market & Neighborhood Farewell: Enjoy a relaxed final morning. Visit the Porta Portese flea market in Trastevere (Rome's famous Sunday market, 6:00–14:00) for vintage finds, antiques, and local atmosphere. Or simply enjoy a long breakfast at a Prati café and revisit your favorite neighborhood spots.
day_by_day.afternoon: Last Gelato & Souvenir Shopping: Spend the early afternoon picking up artisan food souvenirs (pasta, olive oil, wine, biscotti) from quality shops on Via Cola di Rienzo near your hotel. Enjoy a final gelato from your favorite gelateria. Pack and prepare for departure.
day_by_day.evening: Departure Preparation / Optional Farewell Dinner: If your departure is the next morning, enjoy a quiet final dinner near the hotel in the Borgo or Prati area — a simple, satisfying Roman meal to close the trip. Early night for a rested departure.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely final Roman breakfast — sit outside at a Prati café, order a sfogliatella or maritozzo con panna alongside your cappuccino. Savor it (€5–8).
meals.lunch: Light lunch or street food from the Porta Portese market area, or a quick pizza al taglio on the way back to the hotel (€8–12).
meals.dinner: Low-key farewell dinner at a neighborhood trattoria in Prati or Borgo — comfort Roman food, local wine, no rush. Budget €20–35 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Porta Portese runs Sunday mornings only — arrive by 9:00 for the best selection before the crowds peak. Keep some budget for quality food souvenirs to bring home. Confirm airport transfer or taxi booking for your departure day. The Leonardo Express from Termini to Fiumicino runs every 30 minutes and takes 32 minutes.

meals.dinner: Ristorante Il Matriciano (Via dei Gracchi) — a Roman institution since 1957, beloved for impeccable traditional cuisine and refined atmosphere.

day_by_day.notes: Arrange private airport transfer in advance. Ask the hotel concierge to confirm all upcoming experience bookings for the week. June in Rome is warm (mid-to-high 20s°C expected), so pack light breathable clothing and sun protection.

day_by_day.morning: Vatican Museums & Sistine Chapel — Private Early-Access Tour. Begin with an exclusive skip-the-line private guided experience through one of the world's greatest art collections: the Gallery of Maps, Raphael Rooms, and the breathtaking Sistine Chapel ceiling by Michelangelo. A private guide ensures an intimate, unhurried experience before the general public crowds arrive.
day_by_day.afternoon: St. Peter's Basilica & Dome Climb. After the museums, cross into St. Peter's Square for a guided tour of the Basilica — Michelangelo's Pietà, Bernini's baldachin, and the papal tombs. Ascend the dome for panoramic views over Rome. Return to the hotel for a midday rest during the hottest part of the afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Trastevere Food & Wine Evening Walk. Be guided through the cobblestone streets of Trastevere sampling authentic Roman street food — supplì, artichokes alla giudia, porchetta, and local wines — as the neighbourhood glows golden in the evening light.

meals.breakfast: Full Italian breakfast at the hotel or at the celebrated Gran Caffè Roma in Prati — freshly baked pastries, cappuccino, and seasonal fruit.
meals.lunch: Elegant lunch at Ristorante Settimio all'Arancio near the Vatican — fresh antipasti, house-made pasta, and a glass of chilled Frascati.
meals.dinner: Included as part of the Trastevere Food & Wine Evening Walk experience; supplement with a final glass of wine at a candlelit Trastevere enoteca such as Enoteca Ferrara.

day_by_day.notes: Book the Vatican private early-access tour well in advance — ideally 2–3 months ahead for June dates. Dress code enforced at St. Peter's: shoulders and knees must be covered.

day_by_day.morning: Borghese Gallery Art Experience — Private Guided Visit. Take a private chauffeured transfer to the Villa Borghese park for an intimate guided tour of the Borghese Gallery. Marvel at Bernini's extraordinary marble sculptures — Apollo and Daphne, The Rape of Proserpina — and Caravaggio's dramatic masterworks in one of Rome's most intimate and exquisite museum settings. Timed entry is strictly limited, ensuring an uncrowded experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Villa Borghese Gardens Exploration & Pincian Hill Terrace. After the gallery, enjoy a leisurely walk through the manicured gardens of Villa Borghese. Ascend to the Pincian Hill terrace for sweeping panoramic views over Piazza del Popolo and Rome's rooftops. Optional: rent a rowing boat on the ornamental lake.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at a top-tier Roman restaurant in the Parioli or Tridente neighbourhood. Recommended: Ristorante Mirabelle at Hotel Splendide Royal — rooftop terrace dining with spectacular views over Rome, celebrated tasting menus, and an exceptional wine cellar.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hotel followed by an espresso at a neighbourhood bar in Prati.
meals.lunch: Refined al fresco lunch at Caffè delle Arti inside the Villa Borghese park — a charming art nouveau café serving seasonal Roman cuisine.
meals.dinner: Ristorante Mirabelle (Via di Porta Pinciana) — rooftop fine dining with panoramic Rome views, seasonal tasting menu, and sommelier-paired wines.

day_by_day.notes: Borghese Gallery tickets are timed and strictly limited to 360 visitors per 2-hour slot — advance booking is absolutely essential, often months ahead. Private chauffeur recommended for the day.

day_by_day.morning: Cooking Class — Handmade Pasta & Tiramisu. Join a small-group hands-on cooking class in a historic Roman kitchen. Under the guidance of a professional Italian chef, master the art of making fresh egg pasta from scratch (tagliatelle, pappardelle), a classic Roman sauce, and the definitive tiramisu. An immersive, convivial, and deeply satisfying culinary experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Campo de' Fiori & Jewish Ghetto Exploration. After the class (and tasting your creations for lunch!), take a leisurely walk through the atmospheric Campo de' Fiori market square and into Rome's ancient Jewish Ghetto. Visit the Great Synagogue of Rome and explore the charming streets, stopping at a pasticceria for Jewish-Roman pastries such as ricotta-filled crostata.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset aperitivo on a rooftop terrace followed by dinner at a celebrated restaurant in the historic centre. Recommended: Ristorante Pierluigi in Piazza de' Ricci — a Roman institution with elegant outdoor seating, exceptional seafood, and a superb wine list.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely hotel breakfast or a stop at Forno Campo de' Fiori for Rome's finest fresh-baked pizza bianca and pastries.
meals.lunch: The dishes prepared during your cooking class — enjoyed together with your classmates and chef, paired with local wine.
meals.dinner: Ristorante Pierluigi (Piazza de' Ricci) — sophisticated alfresco Roman dining, celebrated for fresh seafood and classic primi.

day_by_day.notes: Confirm the cooking class meeting point with the provider — many classes are held in private historic apartments or culinary studios near the centre. Wear comfortable clothes you don't mind getting flour on!

day_by_day.morning: Testaccio Market & Offal Food Tour. Immerse yourself in authentic Roman culinary culture at the Testaccio covered market — the historic working-class heart of Roman gastronomy. With an expert food guide, taste suppli, mortadella, aged pecorino, and the neighbourhood's celebrated offal specialities (trippa, coda alla vaccinara). Explore the market stalls and meet the passionate vendors who supply Rome's finest restaurants.
day_by_day.afternoon: Palatine Hill, Roman Forum & Colosseum — Private Guided Tour. Transfer to the ancient heart of Rome for a private guided tour of the Palatine Hill (with its stunning imperial palace ruins and gardens), the Roman Forum, and the Colosseum. A luxury private guide brings the ancient city vividly to life, with skip-the-line VIP access throughout.
day_by_day.evening: Aperitivo with a view at a rooftop bar near the Colosseum, followed by dinner at a refined restaurant in the Testaccio or Aventine neighbourhood — the authentic Roman culinary quarter.

meals.breakfast: Light breakfast at the hotel before the early market tour.
meals.lunch: Tastings are included throughout the Testaccio Market Food Tour; supplement with a sit-down lunch at Flavio al Velavevodetto — a beloved Testaccio trattoria carved into the ancient Monte Testaccio.
meals.dinner: Ristorante Checchino dal 1887 (Via di Monte Testaccio) — Rome's most historic fine-dining institution, celebrated since 1887 for refined Roman cuisine and an extraordinary wine cellar of 500+ labels.

day_by_day.notes: The Testaccio Market tour is best enjoyed on a weekday morning when vendors are at their most lively. Book Colosseum private access well in advance for June. Checchino dal 1887 reservations should be made at least 2 weeks ahead.

day_by_day.morning: Galleria Doria Pamphilj & Palazzo Altemps. Begin with a private visit to the magnificent Galleria Doria Pamphilj — a hidden gem of a private noble palace housing Velázquez's portrait of Pope Innocent X, Caravaggio, Titian, and Raphael, largely undiscovered by mass tourism. Continue to the nearby Palazzo Altemps for its serene collection of ancient Greek and Roman sculpture.
day_by_day.afternoon: Piazza Navona, Pantheon & Tridente Luxury Shopping. Stroll through Piazza Navona to admire Bernini's Fountain of the Four Rivers, then walk to the awe-inspiring Pantheon (pre-booked timed entry). Explore the elegant Via Condotti and surrounding streets for Rome's finest luxury boutiques — Valentino, Bulgari, Fendi — and visit the Spanish Steps.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell pre-dinner cocktails at the Stravinskij Bar at the Hotel de Russie — one of Rome's most glamorous and storied hotel bars — followed by a grand farewell dinner at a Michelin-starred restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Indulgent breakfast at the hotel or at Antico Caffè Greco on Via Condotti — Rome's oldest café (1760), a cultural landmark.
meals.lunch: Elegant lunch at Ristorante La Rosetta near the Pantheon — Rome's finest seafood restaurant, beloved by gourmets for decades.
meals.dinner: Il Pagliaccio (Via dei Banchi Vecchi) — Rome's most celebrated two-Michelin-star restaurant, offering a breathtaking tasting menu of creative Italian haute cuisine with exceptional wine pairings.

day_by_day.notes: Reserve Il Pagliaccio at least 4–6 weeks in advance — it is one of Rome's most sought-after tables. Dress code is smart-elegant. The Pantheon now requires timed entry tickets — book online in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely final morning in Rome. Enjoy a long, indulgent breakfast at the hotel. Take a final unhurried walk through the Borgo district and along the Tiber, revisiting your favourite corners of the neighbourhood. Visit the Castel Sant'Angelo museum if time permits — its rooftop terrace offers one of the most romantic views in Rome.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on departure time: last-minute gift shopping at the artisan boutiques of Via della Conciliazione or Prati neighbourhood (fine Italian leather goods, wines, gourmet foods, art prints). Private chauffeur transfer to the airport with ample time before your flight.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Rome. Arrivederci, Roma.

meals.breakfast: Luxurious final breakfast at the hotel — request a special send-off spread from the kitchen.
meals.lunch: Light farewell lunch at a Prati neighbourhood favourite such as Osteria dell'Angelo — simple, perfect Roman classics: cacio e pepe, abbacchio, tiramisu.
meals.dinner: Airport or in-flight dining.

day_by_day.notes: Arrange private chauffeur airport transfer the evening before. Allow at least 2.5–3 hours before your flight departure given Rome traffic in June. Ask the hotel to store luggage if checkout is before your transfer time. Consider purchasing a bottle of fine Lazio wine or Roman artisan products as a souvenir.
